barguna-shutki.desc: In the dry months, fishing families along Barguna's coast dry fish on bamboo racks in the sun. Loitta, chhuri, prawns and small fish are common. The dried fish is cooked into a strong, spicy bhuna or mashed into bhorta. Buying directly from camps gets you cleaner, fresher stock.

tengragiri-forest.desc: Tengragiri is a protected coastal mangrove forest stretching along Barguna's shoreline. Keora and other mangrove trees grow along tidal channels, and the forest shelters deer, wild boar and many birds. The Sonakata eco-park on its edge provides walking paths and a starting point for visits. It is often described as the country's second-largest mangrove after the Sundarbans.
blocks: How to get there
From Taltoli, take a motorbike to Sonakata eco-park.
Good to know
Stay on trails; carry mosquito repellent and avoid visiting in heavy weather.

taltoli-rakhine-temple.desc: Taltoli has long been home to a Rakhine community, and its Buddhist temple is a centre of village life. The temple holds Buddha statues and shows Rakhine architectural details. Around it, Rakhine homes and small shops sell handwoven cloth. A visit here pairs well with the Taltoli beaches and forest.
blocks: How to get there
In Taltoli upazila, reachable by road from Amtali.
Good to know
Remove shoes before entering and ask before taking photos.

glance: Hotels near Patharghata fish landing centre
patharghata-ilish.desc: Patharghata is a major fish landing centre on the Bishkhali, where trawlers return from the Bay with hilsa and other sea fish. In season the docks are a frenzy of boats, baskets and auctioneers. Local hotels cook the fish fresh, fried or with mustard. It is the freshest hilsa you will find.
blocks: Good to know
Respect the government hilsa fishing ban periods.

glance: 260 km to Barguna by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
bibi-chini-mosque.desc: Bibi Chini Mosque stands on a mound in Bibi Chini village of Betagi. It is linked to Shah Neyamat Ullah, a saint who is said to have come here in 1659 during Shah Shuja's governorship of Bengal. The mosque is a protected monument of the Department of Archaeology. Its simple form and rural setting give it a peaceful feel.
blocks: How to get there
From Barguna, go by bus to Betagi, then motorbike or rickshaw about 10 km to Bibi Chini.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

glance: 260 km to Barguna by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
bihanga-island.desc: This island in the Baleshwar river, between Patharghata and the Sundarbans shore, was known to locals for years as Dhanseer Char, after the plants that once grew on it. It was later renamed Bihanga Dwip, 'bird island'. Sandbanks and grass draw waders and other birds, and from its edge you look straight across the river to the Sundarbans. There are no facilities, and it is reached only by hired trawler, so a visit feels like a small expedition. Local tourism listings for Patharghata now name it alongside Haringhata and Laldia.
blocks: How to get there
From Barguna go by bus to Patharghata, then hire a trawler from a riverside village ghat to the island; ask locally for the current boarding point.
Good to know
Go with local boatmen, wear a life jacket and return well before dark. Avoid the river in rough weather or during storm signals. Bring binoculars in winter.

rakhine-water-festival.desc: Around mid-April, Rakhine communities in Taltoli and the wider coast celebrate their New Year with Sangrai. Young men and women throw water at each other from decorated pandals, a ritual of washing away the past year's misfortune. Temples hold prayers, and homes prepare special food. Visitors are welcome to watch respectfully.
blocks: Good to know
Ask before joining the water play and don't photograph without consent.

glance: 260 km to Barguna by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
laldia-beach.desc: Laldia beach sits at the mouth of the Baleshwar and Bishkhali rivers, right beside the Laldia forest. Sea on one side, forest on the other and a strip of sand in between is what makes it unusual. Casuarina trees have been planted along the shore, and both sunrise and sunset can be watched from here. A wooden foot trail through the Harinbaria forest near Haringhata has been extended towards the beach, so you can walk in through the trees. It sees far fewer visitors than Kuakata.
blocks: How to get there
From Barguna take a bus to Patharghata, then a motorbike to Laldia. You can also walk about two hours from Haringhata through the forest.
Good to know
Combine it with Haringhata forest. Wear comfortable shoes for the trail and carry water and snacks; facilities are few.

glance: 260 km to Barguna by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
shuvo-sondha-beach.desc: Shuvo Sondha lies in Nishanbaria union of Taltoli, where the Payra, Bishkhali and Baleshwar rivers flow into the Bay of Bengal. A few kilometres of sand are backed by casuarina groves planted against erosion. Opened as a tourist spot in 2017, it is still quiet compared with Kuakata. Sunsets over the water are the main attraction.
blocks: How to get there
From Barguna town, go by road to Taltoli via Amtali, then motorbike to Nishanbaria.
Good to know
Facilities are basic, with few toilets or restaurants; carry water and snacks. Do not swim: rip currents have caused drownings here.

glance: 260 km to Barguna by road, 7–9 hours by bus or car
haringhata-forest.desc: Haringhata is a planted coastal forest near the mouth of the Bishkhali in Patharghata. Wooden walkways lead among the trees, and the name hints at the deer that live here. On its edges lie sandy shores and views of the meeting rivers. It sees mostly local visitors.
blocks: How to get there
From Barguna, go by road to Patharghata, then auto or motorbike to Haringhata.
Good to know
Carry water and mosquito repellent; avoid the forest late in the day.
